Ascott to open 245-key Somerset Clarke Quay Singapore this December
article:
The Ascott Limited, CapitaLand Investment’s wholly-owned hospitality arm, will open Somerset Clarke Quay Singapore on Dec 15.

Located at 3 Clarke Quay, the 245-key development will be the second Somerset-branded property in Singapore. Room sizes range from 18 to 67 sq m (194 to 721 sq ft), with “residential-style amenities designed to provide practical comforts of home”, said Ascott.

The rooms are available across 12 categories, from king and twin rooms to one- and two-bedroom layouts.

Selected room types feature kitchenettes with cooking facilities, a refrigerator, microwave, kitchenware and tableware. In-room washer-dryers provide added convenience for longer stays, while daily housekeeping services are also available.

The property will also offer “Wellness Tech” themed rooms across studio, suite and loft configurations, with features centred on guests’ well-being. These include a curated pillow menu, blackout curtains, air purifiers and in-room water dispensers.

Rooms with a “Family Explorer” theme will also be available, with designs inspired by Cubby, Somerset’s mascot, and the otters of the Singapore River. The rooms come with bunk beds, “Explorer” welcome kits, interactive discovery packs and family-friendly amenities.

Beyond the rooms, family-oriented facilities include a 7.8m-tall Mama Otter Slide, designed by playground specialist Playpoint, and the Kids’ Cloud Forest, an indoor play space for children.

Other amenities comprise an indoor gymnasium and swimming pools.

Fort Canning MRT Station is adjacent to the property, while lifestyle destinations such as Boat Quay , Robertson Quay and Fort Canning Park are within 1km.

title: Seller makes $2.5 mil profit on sale of four-bedder at Astrid Meadows
article:
Topping the list of profitable condo resale deals during the week of Nov 3 to 10 was a four-bedroom unit at Astrid Meadows , a freehold development in District 10.

The 3,800 sq ft unit on the second floor changed hands for $8.88million ($2,337 psf) on Nov 5, netting the owner a profit of $2.48 million, or 38.8%. The seller, who had purchased the apartment in July 2017 for $6.4 million ($1,684 psf), saw an annualised gain of 4.3% over a nine-year period.

The absolute profit is the largest among resale deals at Astrid Meadows this year. The development has seen five other apartments change hands in 2026, with caveats showing that four of these were lucrative transactions. These sellers earned surpluses ranging between $200,000 and $2.18 million.

However, the biggest gain made at the condo was the $4.95 million profit when a 2,745 sq ft four-bedder was transacted in March 2024. The seller had purchased the unit for $2.1 million in November 2004 and later sold it for $7.05 million.

Completed in 1990, Astrid Meadows is a 208-unit development along Coronation Road West. The sprawling development features several blocks housing one- to five-bedders measuring between 872 and 6,771 sq ft.

The development is surrounded by landed residential enclaves, including the Leedon Park, Oei Tiong Ham Park , and the Bin Tong Park Good Class Bungalow areas. Nearby amenities include retail offerings at Holland Village , a five-minute drive away.

The second most profitable condo resale transaction during the week took place at The Gardens At Bishan . A four-bedroom unit measuring 1,582 sq ft at the 99-year leasehold development was sold for $2.8million ($1,770 psf) on Nov 6.

The seller had bought the unit from the developer in January 2002 for about $768,000 ($485 psf). As a result, the seller raked in a gain of $2.03 million. This translates to a 265% profit,  or 11% annualised over nearly 25 years.

The gain is the second-largest recorded to date at The Gardens At Bishan. It falls about $240,000 short of the top profit of $2.27 million from the sale of a 2,336 sq ft, four-bedroom unit in January 2024.

The Gardens At Bishan is located along Sin Ming Walk in District 20. Completed in 2004, it comprises four 20-storey blocks. There are a total of 756 residences, ranging from one-bedders of 861 sq ft to four-bedders of 2,756 sq ft.

The development is about a five-minute walk to Bright Hill MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line. It is also close to several nature reserves and parks, including Windsor Nature Park, Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park and Lower Peirce Reservoir Park.

Apart from the unit sold on Nov 6, caveats show that The Gardens At Bishan has seen 17 other resale deals this year, with 16 of those being in the black. The sellers reaped gains ranging from $286,000 to $1.98 million.

Meanwhile, Smart Suites , a freehold development on Sims Avenue, saw the least profitable resale deal this week. The owner of a two-bedroom unit on the first floor incurred a loss of about $300,000 (24%) when it changed hands for $950,000($1,261 psf) on Nov 3.

The seller had bought the 753 sq ft apartment in a new sale for $1.25 million ($1,659 psf) in April 2012. Given the holding period of nearly 15 years, the loss thus works out to 1.7% on an annualised basis.

The Nov 3 deal now marks the steepest loss at Smart Suites, exceeding the previous record shortfall of $135,000. That came from the January 2022 sale of a 936 sq ft, two-bedroom unit for $1.05 million ($1,121 psf).

The 72-unit Smart Suites was built in 2014. The boutique development has a single five-storey block with one- to three-bedroom apartments of between 452 and 1,119 sq ft.

Located off Sims Avenue in District 14, the apartment is a five-minute walk from Aljunied MRT Station on the East-West Line, which is one stop away from the Paya Lebar MRT interchange for the Circle Line.

Other amenities in the vicinity include eateries and shops in the Geylang area, the Paya Lebar cluster of malls (PLQ Mall, Paya Lebar Square and SingPost Centre), and lifestyle offerings in the Joo Chiat-Katong enclave.

Apart from the unit sold on Nov 3, Smart Suites has seen only one other resale transaction this year, based on caveats lodged. A three-bedder measuring 1,119 sq ft fetched $1.28 million on Oct 7, netting the seller a profit of around $73,000.

title: Fresh price high of $2,825 psf at Sommerville Park freehold condo with three-bedder’s resale
article:
Sommerville Park — a freehold condo in prime District 10 — emerged the top performer among private non-landed residential developments that set new psf-price benchmarks during the period of Nov 3 to 10.

It posted a fresh record of $2,825 psf on Nov 4 with the sale of a 1,302 sq ft three-bedder for $3.68 million.

That is the first time a unit at Sommerville Park has transacted above the $2,800 psf threshold. The psf price is almost 7% higher than the development’s former peak of $2,649 psf, established by the resale of another 1,302 sq ft, three-bedroom unit for $3.45 million on July 28.

Completed in 1985, Sommerville Park has 396 condo units alongside 57 strata landed houses. The units are housed in four residential towers, comprising a mix of one- to three-bedders, while the landed residences include townhouses and two-storey maisonettes.

The condo is within a 2km radius of several schools, including Raffles Girls’ Primary School, Nanyang Primary School and Hwa Chong Institution.

In terms of absolute quantum, the most expensive transaction at the development thus far is the resale of a 2,799 sq ft three-bedder, which fetched $5.5 million ($1,965 psf) in January 2024.

Second among the week’s top project highs was 99-year leasehold condo Meraprime .

The development achieved a fresh price peak of $2,353 psf when a 1,313 sq ft, four-bedroom unit changed hands for $3.09 million on Nov 4.

This edges out Meraprime’s prior record of $2,305 psf that was set by the sale of an 840 sq ft two-bedder for $1.94 million about two months prior on Sept 10.

Located along Jalan Bukit Ho Swee in District 3, Meraprime is a 213-unit condo that was completed in 2006. Housed within a single 36-storey residential tower, units range from two- to four-bedders of 840 to 1,313 sq ft.

The development sits opposite Tiong Bahru Plaza , which offers retail and dining options, and is a four-minute walk from Tiong Bahru MRT Station.

Resale prices at Meraprime have been on an upward trajectory over the past five years, based on resale caveats tabulated by EdgeProp Singapore. Its one-year average resale price has climbed from $1,808 psf in November 2021 to about $2,044 psf as of November this year — up by 13%.

Back in District 10, Chatelet also hit a new psf-price high during the week.

The freehold condo notched a fresh price benchmark of $2,282 psf when a 980 sq ft two-bedder fetched $2.24 million on Nov 5.

This beats Chatelet’s former high of $2,180 psf. That was established earlier this year on May 25 when a 1,582 sq ft, three-bedroom unit was sold for $3.45 million.

Chatelet is a boutique condo located on Margoliouth Road. Completed in 1993, it has just 45 units, comprising two- and three-bedders measuring between 958 and 1,808 sq ft.

The development has seen a relatively low level of resale transactions, logging a total of three thus far this year.

Excluding the Nov 5 deal, the other two involved three-bedroom units measuring 1,507 and 1,582 sq ft, which were priced at $2,123 and $2,180 psf, respectively.

No psf-price lows were recorded for the week.

title: Commercial unit at freehold Sai Ho Building offered at auction for $12.5 mil
article:
A strata commercial unit at Sai Ho Building — a freehold mixed-use development along Upper Serangoon Road — was put on the block at ETC’s property auction on Nov 18 in an owner’s sale.

The 4,424 sq ft unit had a guide price of $12.5 million, which translates to $2,826 psf.

This is the first time the property has gone up for auction, says Joy Tan, head of auction & sales at ETC.

ETC declined to comment on the outcome of the auction in response to EdgeProp Singapore’s queries.

The ground-floor unit comes with a basement, which is accessible via an internal staircase.

The unit is leased to an international school until February 2031. As a commercial property, it is not subject to additional buyer’s stamp duty.

Tan expects the property to attract investor interest, given its existing tenancy. “Buyers can enjoy immediate rental income without the need to source for a new tenant,” she says.

Its freehold tenure also offers long-term ownership and the potential for capital appreciation, adds Tan.

Located in District 19, Sai Ho Building is a boutique development with seven commercial units and eight residential apartments. It was completed in 1986.

The property is located within a 10-minute walk from Serangoon MRT Station, as well as lifestyle and retail options at Nex shopping mall.

Based on caveats lodged, the latest transaction of a freehold strata commercial unit on Upper Serangoon Road was for a 1,421 sq ft property at Yeley Building that fetched $3 million ($2,111 psf) on March 31.

Before that, four strata commercial units — three retail properties and one office — at Upper Serangoon Shopping Centre changed hands in 2024.

The three retail units, spanning 183 to 248 sq ft, were sold at $1,913 to $2,343 psf, or between $350,000 and $580,000.

The office unit, measuring 205 sq ft, was sold for $550,000, or $2,689 psf.

title: Inside two landed homes designed for the tropical climate and ageing in place
article:
In Singapore’s harsh tropical climate, understanding a site’s orientation and exposure to the elements is an important starting point in residential design, says Diong Fuhan, principal architect and founder of Quod Architects.

“Any house should be designed to accommodate the heat and monsoon season,” she says.

The firm’s approach is reflected in two of its recently completed residential projects in District 15: The Angled House, a three-storey detached house, and House of Grids, a corner terraced house.

The clients for both projects are couples approaching retirement age. As a result, in addition to climate considerations, the projects had another design priority: adapting the homes to the changing needs of their occupants while supporting ageing in place.

Revamping a family home

The Angled House was originally built in 2003. It has served as the family home for the owners for over 20 years, though their grown children have since moved out.

The couple brought on Quod Architects to renovate the home to better fit their current needs while also remedying existing pain points.

One such pain point was the lack of shade from the sun. The home’s northwest orientation meant that the front of the property received strong afternoon sun, says Diong. The insufficient shade often resulted in overly warm interiors.

To mitigate this, a distinctive slanted façade was introduced to shield the interiors from the western sun while providing greater privacy from the street.

The angled elements extend to the second storey, forming bay windows that frame the master bedroom and family area.

Beyond responding to the site’s weather conditions, the renovation of The Angled House also focused on adapting the home to the family’s changing needs, says Diong.

Despite being empty-nesters, the homeowners wanted the house to accommodate gatherings, given their active involvement in church and frequent visits from their children and grandchildren, she adds.

Creating communal spaces

To that end, the renovation focused largely on reconfiguring the interiors to create larger communal spaces.

An open, connected layout — linking the living and dining areas with the dry kitchen — was achieved by removing some of the columns running through the middle of the house and reinforcing others.

Built-in cabinetry was introduced within the living areas to provide guests with dedicated spaces to store their belongings, while also doubling as additional seating.

On the attic floor, two existing rooms were combined by removing the partition walls, creating a single open space for church cell group gatherings and visits from family members, shares Diong.

The space also incorporates a flexible guest room. On top of that, a skylight was introduced to bring natural light into the attic.

“The house is designed around a more temporal kind of multigenerational space,” explains Diong. “While their children live overseas or independently, the homeowners want to maintain space for them.”

Additionally, The Angled House’s design can help the homeowners age in place, with features intended to support their comfort and mobility over time.

These include corridors measuring at least 1.2m wide to accommodate wheelchair usage, if required, in the future.

A lift was also installed to improve accessibility between floors for family members of all ages.

Climate-conscious design for easier living

Meanwhile, at House of Grids, climate considerations were approached differently. The design here balanced the homeowners’ vision of an “urban resort” with their practical needs as they age, says Diong.

Quod Architects undertook the design of the three-storey house occupying a 2,400 sq ft plot, with works completed in March this year.

According to Diong, the house was designed for a couple in their fifties who wanted to feel as though they were returning to a resort each time they came home to their corner terraced house.

Here, too, the west-facing orientation meant that mitigating the afternoon sun was a key consideration.

Warm-toned frames and vertical fins form the grid-like structures that give the house its name, with the fins also serving a practical purpose by breaking up direct sunlight.

Balconies with planters along their edges were incorporated to create a “green veil” that provides shade and reduces heat gain, helping to keep the interiors cool.

Diong describes the design approach as a form of “modern vernacular” architecture, drawing on traditional design elements such as large roofs that provide shelter from heat and rain, and high ceilings that promote natural ventilation.

The latter is illustrated in the main living space on the first floor, where the dining area features a double-volume ceiling. Besides allowing for more light and airflow, the space serves as the heart of the home’s layout, connecting the common areas with the private floors above.

“These features remain relevant in Singapore’s tropical climate, as they help to keep the home comfortable while addressing the heat and rain,” says Diong.

These climate-conscious features also reduce the need for blinds and curtains, which means minimising upkeep for the older homeowners, shares Diong.

Maintenance considerations similarly informed the choice of colours and materials throughout the house. A darker palette was selected for the façade to make water stains and weathering from monsoon rain and prolonged exposure to the elements less visible.

“We opted for durable materials and finishes that can withstand wear and tear over time,” explains Diong.

Homes for the next chapter

Although both projects were designed for couples approaching retirement age, their different family arrangements and aspirations informed the distinct approaches, says Diong.

“Both projects organise their spaces around the family, but their habits and living arrangements are different,” she notes.

She adds that growing environmental awareness has also brought greater attention to climate-conscious design, with homeowners placing more emphasis on how their homes can respond to Singapore’s tropical conditions while remaining comfortable and practical over the longer term.

title: ISDN: After 9M Profit Surge, CGS Raises Forecasts by 20–33% — But Cuts Target Price
article:
ISDN Holdings’ 9M2026 results were already strong, but management’s latest presentation provided an even more interesting datapoint: business momentum apparently strengthened further in October.

For 9M2026,

• revenue rose 24.3% year on year to S$397.5 million
•
gross profit climbed 30% to S$100.9 million

•

•
PATMI surged 435% to S$19.1 million.

•

Industrial automation was the main driver, with revenue rising 36.7%.
Semiconductor revenue jumped 52.2% to S$128.3 million, while medical-equipment revenue more than doubled to S$34.6 million.

ISDN

Share price:
$0.51

Target:
$0.95

CGS International analyst William Tng said the results represented a “material outperformance”.
The S$19.1 million 9M PATMI had already reached 95% of CGS’s previous full-year forecast and 102% of Bloomberg consensus.

As a result, CGS raised its FY26, FY27 and FY28 EPS forecasts by
33.0%, 29.9% and 19.6%
, respectively.
Its new PATMI forecasts are S$26.9 million for FY26, S$29.5 million for FY27 and S$30.8 million for FY28.

ISDN managing director CK Teo and CFO Christine Ho at the 3Q2026 hybrid briefing: "“ISDN delivered a strong performance in the first nine months of 2026, with record revenue and a significant improvement in profitability."

Strong order book

Management’s comments suggest even CGS’s revised FY26 number may not be especially aggressive.

Managing director Teo Cher Koon said October was strong while

the order book continued to grow, with some orders flowing into 2027.
When an investor suggested FY26 profit could reach S$28 million to S$30 million, however, Teo declined to endorse the estimate: “I don't want to speculate.”

There is an important qualification.

ISDN’s normal delivery lead time had been around three months, but Teo said it is getting longer because of supply-chain constraints.
Thus, some of the order-book growth reflects longer fulfilment times rather than pure demand growth.

Still, management expects 1H2027 to remain strong although Teo remains cautious about 2H2027 because semiconductors are cyclical.

Hydropower catalyst approaching

The two new mini-hydropower plants also are close to commercial operation.

Asked what remained to be done, Teo said mainly “administrative nitty-gritty stuff”.
Asked when the full S$14 million annual recurring net cash income from the enlarged five-plant portfolio should kick in, his answer: “Next year.”
(This is group/project-level recurring net cash income, not fully attributable to ISDN shareholders).

CGS sees hydropower as one possible re-rating catalyst if its profit contribution exceeds expectations.
Other catalysts include stronger China growth and a stronger semiconductor recovery.

Meanwhile, management disclosed a potentially sizeable renewable-energy pipeline: ISDN is discussing several solar projects totalling roughly
100MW to 200MW
, although these remain preliminary.

Earnings up, target price down

Interestingly, despite sharply upgrading earnings, CGS cut its target price from
S$1.05 to S$0.95
.

The reason is valuation.

CGS previously valued ISDN at around 21 times earnings.
It has now reduced that to
14 times
, based on ISDN’s FY23–FY26 average P/E, while rolling its valuation forward to FY28.
At the recent share price of S$0.51, CGS’s target still implies 86% upside

CGS forecasts ISDN trading at just
8.6 times FY26 earnings
and
7.8 times FY27 earnings
at S$0.51.

title: Retiring in 10 Years? Here’s How to Build Your Portfolio Today
article:
Are you planning to retire at 60?
If you are 50 today, you have another 10 years to get your finances in order.
Let’s say you need S$4,000 a month to cover your expenses in retirement.
That works out to S$48,000 a year.
Your actual spending will depend on the lifestyle you want.
Food, utilities and insurance are part of the picture.
You will also need to budget for healthcare, travel and rising living costs.
CPF LIFE
payouts and rental income, if you have them, can help cover some of these expenses.
For example, if you receive S$2,000 a month from these sources, you will need another S$2,000 from your investments.
That is S$24,000 a year.
At a 4% yield, you will need S$600,000 in investments to generate that income.
But this is only an estimate.
Dividends can fall, and you may have to sell some investments to make up the shortfall.
Building Block #1: Quality Singapore Dividend Stocks
For dividend income, I would look at these three local dividend names –
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited
(SGX: O39), or OCBC,
Sheng Siong Group Ltd
(SGX: OV8) and
Singapore Technologies Engineering Ltd
(SGX: S63), or ST Engineering.
OCBC’s net profit hit a record S$6.24 billion for the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), 10% higher than a year ago.
It paid an interim dividend of S$0.47 per share for 1H2026, up from S$0.41, which translates to a trailing yield of 3.8% as at 17 November 2026.
Sheng Siong’s net profit rose 8.1% year on year (YoY) to S$125.5 million in 9M2026, as revenue grew 9.9% to S$1.3 billion.
The supermarket operator paid an interim dividend of S$0.0375 per share for 1H2026, up from S$0.032 a year earlier.
At a share price of S$2.29 on 17 November 2026, Sheng Siong offered a 3.3% dividend yield.
ST Engineering does not report profit in its nine-month update, but its revenue grew 10% YoY to S$10.0 billion in 9M2026.
Its order book reached a record S$37.7 billion as at 30 September 2026, and it has declared S$0.14 per share in interim dividends for the first three quarters of 2026.
That translates to a yield of 2.7% at a share price of S$8.86 as at 17 November 2026.
I would rather have a yield of around 3% that the company can maintain than an 8% yield that may not last.
Over time, dividend increases can help, too, as living costs rise.
Building Block #2: REITs for Recurring Income
Real estate investment trusts (REITs)
offer another way to earn income from property without having to buy one yourself.
But don’t look at the distribution yield alone.
Check whether the distribution per unit (DPU) has been growing, how much of the properties are occupied and whether rents are going up when leases are renewed, known as rental reversion.
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust
(SGX: C38U), or CICT, which owns retail and commercial properties, ticks these boxes.
Its DPU rose 7.1% YoY to S$0.0602 in 1H2026, and its portfolio was 96.1% occupied as at 30 September 2026.
Rents on renewed leases rose 4.6% for retail and 7.1% for office in 9M2026.
Another CapitalLand REIT is
CapitaLand Ascendas REIT
(SGX: A17U), or CLAR, which focuses on industrial and business spaces.
CLAR’s occupancy was lower at 90.1%, up from 89.1% three months earlier, with rental reversion of 9.0% for 9M2026.
Parkway Life REIT
(SGX: C2PU), or PLife, invests in healthcare properties.
Its DPU grew 13.4% YoY to S$0.131 in 9M2026, helped mainly by higher rents from its three Singapore hospitals.
High borrowing costs or refinancing at less favourable rates can eat into distributions, so check leverage too.
CICT’s aggregate leverage was 39.7% as at 30 September 2026, CLAR’s was 41.8% after its latest acquisitions, and PLife’s gearing was 34.8%.
Spreading your investments across different property sectors can help.
Relying too heavily on REITs for retirement income could still leave your portfolio exposed if the property market weakens.
Building Block #3: Growth Investments to Fight Inflation
You still need growth investments, even with retirement 10 years away.
You could spend another 20 to 30 years in retirement, so your savings need to keep growing.
The
State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
(SGX: S27) is one option.
The exchange-traded fund (ETF) tracks large US companies across different industries, so you don’t have to pick individual stocks.
But share prices can fall sharply, even when retirement is close. You need to decide how much risk you can take without being forced to sell when prices are down.
Building Block #4: Cash and Lower-Risk Investments
You don’t need to put every dollar into the stock market.
Keep some money in the bank, fixed deposits,
Singapore Treasury bills
(T-bills) or Singapore Savings Bonds for expenses that may come up.
It’s also good to have some savings set aside for emergencies.
That way, if the market takes a tumble, you won’t have to sell your stocks just to pay the bills.
But don’t leave too much money sitting around either.
Prices will keep rising, and your savings still need to last through retirement.
How I Would Structure a Portfolio with 10 Years to Retirement
For someone with moderate risk tolerance, one possible allocation is:
Asset Class
Allocation
Singapore dividend stocks
30%
Singapore REITs
20%
Diversified equity ETFs / growth stocks
25%
Bonds and lower-risk investments
15%
Cash
10%
Total
100%
Adjust these weights based on your risk appetite and how much income you expect from CPF LIFE and other sources.
You can continue investing regularly and reinvest dividends rather than relying on them for income.
In the few years leading to retirement, think about how you will draw on your savings.
Your CPF payouts, dividends and other withdrawals should work together to support your retirement spending.
The Biggest Mistakes to Avoid Before Retirement
Avoid chasing speculative stocks or unusually high yields to catch up; a steep market loss close to retirement could severely set you back.
While cash feels safe, inflation will erode its purchasing power over a 20- to 30-year retirement.
You must also guard against sequence-of-returns risk: if the market tumbles just as you retire, selling investments that have fallen in value to cover living expenses locks in your losses and leaves you short when markets recover.
Get Smart: Make the Next 10 Years Count
A decade may seem like a long time, but it will pass quickly.
The aim is to build a portfolio that can provide income when you stop working while still giving your savings room to grow.
As retirement gets closer, you can adjust your investments based on how much income you need and how much you already receive from CPF or other sources.

Each company’s fiscal year ends on 31 March, so the first half of FY2027 (1HFY2027) covers the six months to 30 September 2026.
Is Singtel’s extra dividend backed by growing profits?
Singtel
owns Optus in Australia, Singtel Singapore, technology services arm NCS and Digital InfraCo, which houses its data centre and AI cloud businesses.
For 1HFY2027, Singtel’s underlying net profit rose 10.4% year on year (YoY) to S$1.5 billion, while operating revenue grew 5.5% to S$7.3 billion.
NCS lifted revenue by 10%, while Digital InfraCo’s revenue climbed 22% after its new DC Tuas data centre began operating in January 2026.
Singtel Singapore was the weak spot, with earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) falling 4.5% as intense price competition weighed on mobile revenue.
The interim dividend rose 9.8% to S$0.09 per share, but its two parts tell different stories.
The core dividend rose 10.9% to S$0.071 and, at 78% of underlying net profit, kept the same payout ratio as a year ago.
On the surface, that is earned growth.
The extra component is a value realisation dividend of S$0.019, up from S$0.018.
It is paid from excess capital freed up by capital recycling, which has unlocked S$6.8 billion since the Singtel28 plan began in 2024, or 75% of its S$9 billion mid-term target.
So where does the risk lie?
First, only about S$2.2 billion of that target remains to be unlocked.
Second, part of the profit growth came from a first-time S$153 million dividend from Gulf Development, in which Singtel holds a small stake.
In June 2026, Singtel sold more than a third of that stake for net proceeds of S$952 million, so investors should not expect the same boost every half.
Third, Singtel plans an extra S$1.2 billion of capital expenditure this fiscal year, mainly on data centres and AI.
Partners and customer prepayments will fund S$0.7 billion, leaving about S$0.5 billion to compete with dividends for cash.
Is SIA’s special dividend making up for a smaller ordinary payout?
SIA
runs full-service carrier Singapore Airlines and low-cost carrier Scoot, flying passengers and cargo worldwide.
Revenue hit a record S$11.3 billion in 1HFY2027, up 16.8% YoY.
Profit, however, went in the opposite direction.
Jet fuel averaged US$171 per barrel, 86.7% higher than a year ago amid the Middle East conflict, while profit attributable to owners fell 43.9% to S$133.9 million.
SIA declared an interim ordinary dividend of S$0.02 and a special dividend of S$0.05, bringing the total to S$0.07.
A year earlier, it paid S$0.05 ordinary and S$0.03 special.
The special dividend rose by two-thirds while the ordinary dividend fell 60%, leaving the total payout 12.5% lower.
Five of the seven cents are special, so most of this payout rests on a one-off decision rather than recurring profit.
Cash flow offers some comfort.
Free cash flow rose 70.2% to S$1.4 billion.
Much of that improvement came from working capital, mainly a smaller outflow to trade creditors, but such movements can reverse.
As at 30 September 2026, SIA held S$8.1 billion in cash and bank balances against S$7.0 billion of borrowings and S$3.0 billion of lease liabilities.
Fuel remains the key swing factor.
SIA says adjusting fares and cargo rates does not fully offset sustained high fuel prices, and an extended conflict could hurt demand for travel and air freight.
Until fuel costs ease, the ordinary dividend is the line to watch.
Get Smart: Put the extra on its own line
When a company pays you more, split the payout into its parts.
Look at the ordinary or core dividend on its own and check it against profit.
Then ask what funds the extra, and whether that source will be there next year.
Singtel’s core dividend grew with profit, though part of that profit came from a Gulf stake it has partly sold.
SIA’s ordinary dividend shrank as profit fell, with the special dividend making up part of the difference.
Here’s the thing: an extra dividend is a gift, not a habit.
If the extra disappeared tomorrow, would you still want to own the stock?

Why does Civmec’s growth look locked in?
Civmec
(SGX: P9D) is an integrated construction and engineering services provider for the energy, resources, infrastructure, and marine and defence sectors.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (1QFY2027), which ended 30 September 2026, revenue rose 70.2% year on year (YoY) to a record A$324.0 million.
The growth came from a significant uplift in activity in its construction division.
Major projects such as BHP’s Port Debottlenecking Project 2 and Iluka Resources’ Eneabba Rare Earths Refinery ramped up during the quarter.
Much of the work ahead is already on the books.
The order book stood at about A$1.4 billion as at 29 October 2026, up from A$1.15 billion a year earlier.
The Australian government has also accepted the baseline schedule for Civmec’s offshore patrol vessel programme through to 2029.
However, the quarterly update carried no cash flow statement or balance sheet, so you won’t be able to tell yet whether cash kept pace with revenue.
What we know is this: Civmec paid A$0.06 per share in dividends for FY2026.
Can Micro-Mechanics keep growing once the rebound fades?
Micro-Mechanics (Holdings)
(SGX: 5DD) makes precision tools and parts used in semiconductor manufacturing.
For its 1QFY2027, which also ended 30 September 2026, revenue rose 45.0% YoY to S$24.2 million, an
all-time quarterly high
.
Consumable Tools, the larger division, lifted sales by 33.7%.
Build-to-Print Precision Components nearly doubled its sales, up 97.5%, on higher bookings and recovery from material delays and shortages a year ago.
That recovery boost will fade as the base normalises.
Higher sales pushed gross margin to a 20-quarter high of 55.0%, from 51.5%.
However, cash lagged.
Operating cash flow of S$4.6 million trailed net profit of S$6.4 million as receivables rose.
Higher capital expenditure then pulled free cash flow down 10.6% to S$3.7 million.
The company still held S$33.3 million in cash and no bank borrowings.
How much of Info-Tech’s growth will last?
Info-Tech Systems Ltd
(SGX: ITS) sells cloud-based business software to more than 28,000 businesses.
For the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), revenue rose 20% YoY to S$42.6 million.
Third-quarter revenue grew 18% to S$15.3 million.
Subscriptions make up about three-quarters of revenue, and that recurring base grew 11% to S$32.2 million.
Services grew far faster.
Sales rose 82% to S$8.6 million on strong demand for the company’s AI-related training courses in Singapore.
Management expects training demand to normalise after an exceptional surge in 4Q2025, which came ahead of the expiry of a S$500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up.
That leaves a high base for the coming quarter.
The update covered revenue only and relied on unaudited management accounts.
While it disclosed no profit or cash flow figures, the CEO pointed to a strong cash position and
no debt
.
Why does Tai Sin’s growth need a closer look?
Tai Sin Electric Limited
(SGX: 500) makes and distributes electrical cables, wires and related products across Southeast Asia.
For the fiscal year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), revenue rose 24.2% YoY to S$597.2 million.
A large part of that growth was bought.
Integra R.E., a renewable energy equipment distributor acquired in November 2025, contributed S$59.8 million.
Without it, revenue would have grown about 11.8%.
Profit moved the other way.
Net profit attributable to shareholders fell 56.8% to S$11.2 million.
The main cause was a S$23.1 million provision for fixed-price cable contracts signed when copper prices were lower.
Further copper price moves could trigger more provisions, or reversals.
The provision is a non-cash charge.
Operating cash flow held up, and free cash flow turned positive at S$9.0 million.
Bank borrowings rose to S$106.2 million from S$84.4 million.
The proposed full-year
dividend
stayed at S$0.0235 per share.
Get Smart: Sort the growth before you count it
A headline growth rate tells you how fast revenue grew, but it does not tell you how much of that growth you can expect again.
Before you buy, split the increase into parts.
Ask how much came from contracts already signed or customers who renew every year.
Then ask how much came from one-off boosts, such as a weak base or an acquisition.
The first kind tends to recur, while the second kind needs replacing every year.
Civmec’s order book and Info-Tech’s subscription base give you some visibility.
Micro-Mechanics’ rebound and Tai Sin’s acquisition will not repeat in the same form.

title: Beyond Nvidia: 3 US AI Adopters Every Singapore Investor Should Watch
article:
Since ChatGPT burst onto the scene in late 2022, heralding the age of artificial intelligence (AI), the surest way to invest in this burgeoning technology was through the main supplier of chips that enable AI to function:
Nvidia Corporation
(NASDAQ: NVDA).
Four years on, Nvidia is no longer the only company investors can look to for
AI exposure
.
Companies that adopt AI to improve their business, be it through increased revenues, lower costs, or strengthening their product/service offerings, can be your way to gain exposure to the AI theme.
We spotlight three such US-listed names that have benefited from the adoption of AI in their day-to-day business.
JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM): The Banking AI Adopter
It might surprise you to learn the first name on our list is one of the biggest banks in the world: JPM.
The bank’s AI use spans back-office automation, client servicing and risk mitigation.
Two applications stand out.
First, it uses a proprietary large language model (LLM) to automate routine tasks such as drafting documents and generating insights, which boosts employee efficiency.
Second, JPM has been leveraging AI to analyse transaction patterns and prevent fraudulent activities, which helps reduce losses and improve security for the assets under its management.
The bank estimates up to $1.5 billion in annual value from its AI initiatives.
Looking ahead, investors should watch for increasing tangible value for JPM’s AI strategy, be it through further cost savings or fewer incidents of fraudulent transactions.
Management has committed to embedding AI agents across the bank’s functions, with the aim of building a connected ecosystem of intelligent, automated processes that elevates the client’s experience.
The key risks is that AI agents can behave unpredictably, for instance by bypassing security controls.
In a bank, that could expose sensitive client data.
Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ: ABNB): Personalising your travel experiences
Wouldn’t it feel great to get help on your trip at any hour, without waiting in a queue for a human agent?
Airbnb is using AI to do exactly that.
Its AI assistant now handles a large share of guest and host queries: in 3Q2026, about 40% of all customer support issues were resolved without a human agent, up from around a third in the previous quarter.
It can help with anything from checking in to finding a nearby restaurant that suits your diet.
Importantly, it is available to customers 24/7, and costs nothing extra – much like having a personal butler.
I can vouch for it, too.
On my last trip, these assistants positively enhanced my experience.
The savings are already visible.
Management cited AI-driven customer support efficiencies, alongside revenue growth and cost discipline, as drivers of its higher profit margin in 3Q2026.
Hence, the adoption of AI has allowed Airbnb to improve the user experience for both hosts and travellers, strengthening the network effect of its platform.
There is more to come.
Airbnb is building its own AI agent to help guests plan and book trips, and plans to start rolling it out in the first half of 2027.
Looking ahead, the main risk is that these AI features become commoditised across competitors, which could diminish these benefits for Airbnb.
Meta Platforms, Inc. (NYSE: META): Better-Placed Advertisements
Lastly, the social media giant that owns WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram has demonstrated how its advertising engine has benefited from AI adoption.
In 3Q2026, ad impressions rose 10% year on year (YoY) and the average price per ad climbed 14%, after double-digit gains in both in 2Q2026.
Meta
credits stronger engagement, better recommendations and more efficient monetisation.
Meta’s personal AI agent, Muse, has also passed 10 million downloads in the US and Canada, helped by its ability to automate mundane tasks such as making reservations and filling in forms.
Monetisation is still at an early stage, with paid tiers at US$20 or US$100 a month, but Muse could give Meta’s revenue and profits a meaningful boost in future.
Meta’s free cash flow does not reflect these AI benefits just yet, as the company is still heavily investing in its AI buildout.
Given the advertising business is already showing the benefits of AI, Meta’s key risk would be its inability to monetise Muse.
Why This Matters for Singapore Investors
You can gain exposure to the AI theme by investing in US-listed companies that are early adopters of AI and are already benefiting financially from AI.
These companies do not carry the same thematic risk as AI infrastructure companies like Nvidia, because AI is one growth driver within a business that is already well established.
That said, do be mindful of currency risks (USD/SGD) and potential portfolio concentration should you invest in these US-listed names.
This concentration risk is especially relevant because broad US exchange-traded funds (ETFs) already hold these names; adding to each company individually raises your overall allocation.
Get Smart: Follow the AI Adopters
Instead of investing in
semiconductor
names, we have highlighted how you can gain exposure to the AI theme through three US-listed AI adopters.
These companies span different industries, and their AI adoption is already producing results.
For JPM and Airbnb, the benefits are showing up as cost savings, while AI is helping Meta’s advertising business grow faster.
The next phase of AI investing could lie with the beneficiaries of AI adoption instead of just relying on names that facilitate the buildout of AI infrastructure.

title: Japan Tobacco hit by US$8.9 bil charge on Russia seizure
article:
(Nov 19): Japan Tobacco Inc will take a ¥1.4 trillion (US$8.9 billion) charge after losing control of its Russian subsidiaries, pushing the cigarette maker to a full-year net loss and slashing its dividend forecast.

The Tokyo-based maker of Winston and Mevius cigarettes now expects an operating loss of ¥368 billion instead of a ¥1 trillion profit, according to a statement on Thursday. The revenue outlook was cut by ¥63 billion to ¥3.8 trillion.

The writedown comes after the Russian government seized all seven of JT’s local subsidiaries, causing the company to lose management control and remove them from its consolidated accounts. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi raised the issue of asset seizures, as well as Russia’s arrest of a Japanese journalist, during a meeting with President Vladimir Putin in China on Wednesday.

JT continued operating in Russia after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine while complying with sanctions, leaving it exposed to a market that accounted for about 10% of group sales and a quarter of adjusted operating profit. As recently as last month, the company said it had maintained a solid leadership position in the country and would remain flexible in deciding how to develop the business.

“We would like to ensure that we learn lessons from this and have discussions around it,” Chief executive officer Takehiko Tsutsui said at an analyst briefing. “We would like to look back at this situation and learn from it so that we could reflect our lessons into our risk management structure.”

JT’s strategy will remain largely unchanged even after the deconsolidation of its Russian business, which the CEO said was making a shrinking contribution to growth. The company will continue investing in key markets and growing what it calls reduced-risk products, such as its Ploom range of heated tobacco devices.

See also: Taiwan tightens short selling curbs to help support stock market

Excluding Russia, JT expects adjusted operating profit to grow at an average rate of more than 10% from 2027 through 2029 on a constant-currency basis.

Shares of JT have plunged about 25% since Russia moved to take control of its assets in the country, erasing almost all of the stock’s gain this year. Putin’s move delivered a blow to Takaichi’s government because the Ministry of Finance is Japan Tobacco’s biggest shareholder.

See also: ArcelorMittal jumps on profit boost from tougher steel curbs

Still, the loss was roughly in line with what analysts had expected, said Naoki Fujiwara, a senior fund manager at Shinkin Asset Management Co, adding that the market “may react positively because the announcement removes some of the uncertainty surrounding the situation”.

Russia’s temporary-administration regime doesn’t formally transfer ownership of the businesses to the state or the administrator, and JT said it still indirectly owns 100% of the affected companies. But the restrictions mean it can no longer exercise shareholder rights or make operating decisions as before, forcing it to deconsolidate the units under IFRS accounting rules.

The chairman, deputy chairman and three representative directors will take a 50% cut in pay for two months, while the representative directors will forgo their fiscal 2026 executive bonuses. JT also halved its year-end dividend forecast to ¥68 a share from ¥136.

Russia has long been one of JT’s most important overseas markets. The company has operated there since 1999 and employs about 4,000 people, with production sites including plants in St Petersburg and Rostov-on-Don. It strengthened its position with the US$1.6 billion acquisition of Donskoy Tabak in 2018 and holds about 41% of Russia’s combustible-cigarette market.

The seizure comes as Putin intensifies moves to take control of foreign-owned businesses. Since September, Russia has placed assets belonging to companies including Nestle SA, Auchan and German grocery chain Metro Cash & Carry under temporary management, part of a broader campaign targeting businesses from countries Moscow considers unfriendly.

The action also adds to worsening ties between Moscow and Tokyo. Japan joined Western sanctions against Russia following the invasion of Ukraine, while the countries remain divided by a decades-old territorial dispute and have never signed a formal peace treaty ending World War II.

title: Deutsche Bank probed by data watchdog as leak fallout spreads
article:
(Nov 19): Deutsche Bank AG is facing an investigation over its handling of client data in a sign of the widening fallout from a massive data breach disclosed this week.

Germany’s largest bank is being probed over whether it had “implemented appropriate technical and organisational measures” to safeguard the files, said Alexander Rossnagel, in charge of data protection in Deutsche Bank’s home state of Hesse.

A spokesman for the lender said it’s cooperating fully with the investigation, which was reported earlier by Handelsblatt.

“We informed the competent data protection authority proactively and on a precautionary basis in October,” the spokesman said. “It is standard practice for the authority to review the matter and request further information following such a notification.”

While the watchdog’s ability to impose a fine is limited, the probe adds to headaches for Deutsche Bank, which is struggling to contain the damage from a constant trickle of stories about its past shortcomings. Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil has said the lender needs to explain the measures it has taken to address the issues raised in the articles.

The coverage has put pressure on chief executive officer Christian Sewing, who took over in 2018 and has turned around the firm after it paid billions of euros in misconduct fines. Sewing said on Thursday that clients have reacted calmly to the leak.

See also: France faces more strikes and protests over cost of living

“I think we have built trust and confidence with our clients, whether it’s on the retail side, private banking, wealth management, corporate clients,” he said at a conference organised by JPMorgan Chase & Co. “The feedback we get, I personally get, from our clients is enormously positive, and therefore we actually don’t see any impact.”

Shares of Deutsche Bank rose 1.4% at 2.34pm in Frankfurt on Thursday, paring losses this week to 8.3%.

Several reports based on the leak contained information about high-profile clients of Deutsche Bank. Sewing has told Handelsblatt that the bank had spoken with a number of clients ahead of the publications and that internal and external investigations showed its systems have not been compromised.

See also: Merck KGaA lifts outlook again on life science strength

Deutsche Bank has said the information contained in the more than 15 million files that were leaked to a consortium of news organisations dates back many years and relates to issues that had mostly been known and discussed with regulators. Still, analysts and lawmakers said they raise questions about governance.

In a note to clients earlier in the week, analysts at Autonomous said data security was the “most pressing” question to answer in the wake of the leaks.

“The publication of millions of documents and emails provides very deep insights into Deutsche Bank’s practices,” said Konstantin von Notz, deputy chairman of the Green Party’s parliamentary group. “The security risks arising from the leak are undoubtedly significant.”

Firms are required to have data loss prevention policies in place which often include blocks on transferring data and alerts when unusual data transfer patterns are detected even among employees with access to the information.

A spokesperson for the ECB declined to comment on whether the watchdog had asked Deutsche Bank for additional information on its data security processes.

The European Central Bank’s general risk assessment requires supervisors to assess whether banks “have controls in place to prevent unauthorised data leakage”, according to published documents. Firms who are found to have lax controls can face higher capital charges. The UK’s financial regulators, which oversee Deutsche Bank’s large London branch, and US authorities also have jurisdiction to request information.

title: Anthropic IPO banks land a hefty US$550 mil fee windfall on record IPO
article:
(Nov 19): Anthropic PBC awarded US$550 million to the Wall Street banks working on its blockbuster IPO — more than they made on SpaceX, the previous title holder for the biggest debut ever.

The artificial intelligence (AI) lab agreed to pay the banks, led by Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Morgan Stanley, a fee of about 67 basis points according to Anthropic’s latest filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, in line with the SpaceX banks’ share of the offering.

The haul would be larger than the US$500 million the banks were paid for SpaceX in its US$86.2 billion IPO.

In both deals, the companies took the unusual step of not paying fees for the so-called over-allotment, also known as a greenshoe.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Morgan Stanley scored the top roles on Anthropic’s IPO, taking the same positions they had for SpaceX. Anthropic’s filing shows another 20 banks, all of which will be given a share of the total raised in the offering.

IPOs on average raise less than US$1 billion per deal, and investment banks typically receive 4% to 7% of the size of the offering. That fee percentage drops sharply for larger debuts, a trade-off that many firms accept in order to land a higher rank in the league tables than their peers.

See also: European retail traders snag US$1.1 bil of Anthropic IPO stock

Thanks in part to SpaceX, Wall Street’s biggest banks hauled in the most revenue from advising on equity offerings in the second quarter since 2021, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Goldman Sachs topped the ranks in the quarter ended Sept 30.

Anthropic and its seven co-founders raised US$107.3 billion in an upsized IPO and concurrent private placement, the largest of all time. The debut is set to mark the first listing by a company focused primarily on developing the most advanced AI models.

title: Alibaba’s revenue beats estimates during China’s AI boom
article:
(Nov 19): Alibaba Group Holding Ltd posted a stronger-than-projected 10% rise in revenue, reflecting the company’s pivotal role in providing computing and services to propel China’s artificial intelligence (AI) development boom.

Revenue grew to 271.52 billion yuan (US$40.7 billion or $52.5 billion) in the September quarter, exceeding the average analyst estimate of 270.5 billion yuan. Net income more than tripled, in part because of gains from investments.

Alibaba faces growing pressure to show it can deliver on AI despite new limits on its access to data centre chips. Washington this week moved to shut down a key loophole that Chinese hyperscalers like Alibaba use to access the advanced chips they need. That’s turning investors more cautious on their growth potential, as well as their ability to train and run next-generation models. Alibaba’s market value stands at roughly US$200 billion ($257.9 billion), less than half its level just over a year ago when investors were betting on it to lead the industry.

It already ranks among the country’s biggest AI spenders, plowing capital into research and data centres to drive a cloud service as well as development of cutting-edge AI models. The company benefits in part from renting cloud computing capacity to tech firms developing artificial intelligence, a business that’s thrived alongside Chinese efforts to match US frontier players OpenAI and Anthropic PBC.

Chief executive officer Eddie Wu pledged more than US$53 billion over a three-year period to build a full suite of services and businesses from models to chips. The company raised about US$10.2 billion from a Hong Kong share sale in August, after Wu said spending would surpass original targets.

See also: Lenovo shares fall after first operating loss since 2017

The company just upgraded its flagship large language model, the Qwen4-Max. The Qwen series is the world’s most downloaded open weight model family. It offers a consumer-facing Qwen App, one of China’s most popular, integrating functions including shopping, navigation, and travel booking, as well as a productivity tool dubbed Qwen Work. And it’s Apple Inc’s partner on AI services in China, set to roll out in December.

Wu in September said T-Head — the chipmaking arm recently approved for an IPO in Hong Kong — will soon roll out China’s most powerful domestic semiconductors. It’s shipped more than 560,000 units of its flagship Zhenwu chips so far. Wu said in September the latest Zhenwu V900, slated for mass production in early 2027, can power frontier-model training.

The e-commerce leader-turned-AI developer has made artificial general intelligence, or AGI, as its primary goal. It is also rapidly expanding its computing power, with Wu setting a target of building more than 20 gigawatts of global data centre capacity globally by 2032.

See also: Tencent’s sales miss estimates in setback for founder’s AI push

Alibaba carried out a major restructuring in March to put most of its AI-related projects into a unified unit named Alibaba Token Hub, led by Wu, to better monetize the technology.

It also adjusted its earnings structure this year to showcase fast-growing sales from AI labs and applications, which rose 16% in the quarter ended in June. But its stock has plunged over 40% since the beginning of the year.

The Hangzhou-headquartered company also faces ongoing litigation in the US seeking to be removed from a blacklist by the US Department of Defense. The company last month won a preliminary injunction in that case.

title: European retail traders snag US$1.1 bil of Anthropic IPO stock
article:
(Nov 19): Anthropic PBC sold US$1.1 billion worth of stock to mom-and-pop investors in the UK and continental Europe as part of the biggest initial public offering (IPO) of all time.

The artificial intelligence (AI) lab sold just over 3.6 million shares to retail investors in the UK and close to 9.7 million shares to those in the European Union, Norway and Switzerland, according to regulatory filings reviewed by Bloomberg News.

Anthropic and its co-founders overcame mounting concerns about the pace of AI spending and turbulent markets to price the IPO above the marketed range and raise a record US$107.3 billion. The company’s debut later on Thursday in New York will make it the first publicly traded major AI lab, and the shares were indicated to open higher in gray market trading.

At the IPO price of US$83 per share, the company and its founders raised about US$300 million and US$801 million, respectively, through the dedicated offerings in Britain and on the continent. That compares to the US$364 million Elon Musk’s SpaceX sold to UK savers and the more than US$600 million it offered to European retail.

In the UK, the company made use of the public-offer platforms regime to access local investors without the need for a separate prospectus. Investment platform RetailBook coordinated the offering, firms including AJ Bell plc, Hagreaves Lansdown and Revolut handling orders.

On the continent, Anthropic launched a regional offer for investors in Germany, Denmark, Finland, France, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland. The offering was arranged by European banks including BNP Paribas SA, Deutsche Bank AG and UBS Group AG and brokers including Trade Republic and Saxo Bank AS.

See also: Anthropic raises US$107.3 bil to top SpaceX’s record debut

title: Japan's central bank chief unfazed by consumption drop, stays open to rate hike
article:
(Nov 19): Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Kazuo Ueda said he expects consumer spending to return to a rising trend, signalling that a recent economic contraction driven by weak consumption won’t dissuade the central bank from raising its benchmark interest rate.

“In addition to a steady increase in nominal wages, we expect the pace of inflation to gradually slow down,” Ueda said in Parliament on Thursday. “The positive cycle from income to spending will be maintained and personal consumption will return to a moderate growth trend.”

Earlier this week, data showed that gross domestic product fell in the third quarter partly due to a drop in consumer spending. Ueda said the data were within expectations, noting that inflation has weighed on pensioners who are not benefitting from higher wages. The governor reiterated that wage hikes are spreading from big companies to smaller ones, and consumer spending is resilient overall.

The governor’s remarks show he is keeping the door open for another rate hike next month, stoking market expectations, with overnight index swaps showing a roughly 84% probability of a hike as of Thursday in Tokyo.

Ueda’s board hit a milestone last month as it acknowledged that underlying inflation had risen to levels in line with the bank’s 2% inflation target for the first time since the introduction of the goal in 2013.

With that assessment, the BOJ has clearly indicated its focus is no longer on coaxing underlying inflation higher but rather on keeping it around the current level. Authorities have repeatedly said there are risks to the upside for inflation.

See also: Japan's Rakuten Bank shares tank as securities arm faces data breach

Data on Friday are expected to show Japan’s key inflation gauge quickened in October to the fastest pace this year. On top of the persistent weakness of the yen, the Iran war is exacerbating Japan’s cost of living crisis by driving up the price of oil. Japan relies heavily on imports of oil, raw materials and food.

Ueda is scheduled to make a speech on Nov 30 before the BOJ delivers its next policy decision on Dec 18.

title: Lenovo shares fall after first operating loss since 2017
article:
(Nov 19): Lenovo Group Ltd shares slid more than 5% after reporting a far larger-than-anticipated loss for the September quarter, reflecting accounting charges and the mounting cost of PC components.

China’s No 1 PC maker reported a net loss of US$640 million versus a year-earlier profit, surpassing average estimates for a loss of US$38 million. Much of that stemmed from fair value changes on derivatives that it booked last quarter. It also posted its first operating loss since 2017 after registering a US$1.9 billion non-cash fair value loss from warrant revaluation.

Lenovo has emerged as one of the beneficiaries of the global artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom. This week, Nvidia Corp hiked its outlook for the next fiscal year on robust demand for its cutting-edge silicon, saying revenue will grow 75%. The Chinese company said revenue hit US$30.2 billion in the three-month period ended September, beating estimates.

However, the soaring cost of memory is compressing margins, while investors worry about the sustainability of long-term data center demand. The high-profile departure of Nvidia’s former chief executive officer Jensen Huang, along with rising costs, competition and debt, have prompted some investors to question the durability of the AI super cycle.

Lenovo’s shares have fallen more than 50% from their peak in September as part of a broader global selloff in AI-related stocks.

The AI momentum is strong and sustainable, Lenovo chairman and CEO Yang Yuanqing said in an interview. “We are seeing this real demand every day.”

See also: Tencent’s sales miss estimates in setback for founder’s AI push

The Trump administration on Monday moved to restrict overseas data centres from providing Chinese AI developers with remote access to advanced US chips and servers, closing a loophole that had allowed them to tap computing power housed outside China. Global AI data centres operate cutting-edge AI servers assembled by brands including Lenovo.

The latest rule has “no significant impact to our business”, Yang said. “We are a global company. We have presence in almost all markets.”

Lenovo also has to navigate a slump in demand for PCs, which remains a key part of its business. Global PC shipments fell 21.2% in the past quarter partly due to rising component prices, according to researchers at Omdia, while Lenovo saw a slightly larger drop of 22.9%.

See also: Chinese AI stocks down as US chip curbs hit labs and hyperscalers

The company is betting on products with AI features to help off set some of the impact.

title: Trump suggests US can sell Blackwell chips to China in future
article:
(Nov 19): US President Donald Trump said that the US could potentially allow the sale of Nvidia Corp’s highly sought Blackwell chips to China in the future, when they are no longer among the most advanced on the market.

“In two years or three years, I would, if I were here, I would say, go ahead. You can now sell Blackwells because they will have something else,” Trump said in an interview with Fox News from Shenzhen, China, where he is attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

“As you know, they are already working on something else that’s going to be superseding the Blackwell chip,” he added. “But in two or three years, I will say, go do the Blackwells because they will be able to do it.” Trump’s term ends in January 2029.

China’s access to artificial intelligence (AI) chips has become a major flashpoint at the summit following the ouster of Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang over an affair with a woman now under investigation by the US government for potentially working with a Chinese spy agency and possibly helping smuggle chips.

The Trump administration earlier this week moved to heighten scrutiny on exports of processors to several countries in a bid to restrict Chinese companies from obtaining remote access to AI chips and servers.

Blackwell chips are central to the technology rivalry between the US and China. The chips’ capabilities would provide a major boost to Beijing’s efforts to rapidly develop AI technology.

See also: Meta to hire new India policy chief to repair frayed ties — Bloomberg

Nvidia under Huang had pushed for the US government to grant permission to sell the chips but the Trump administration never agreed to that request, instead allowing the sale of processors known as H200 that are less advanced.

“Look, the only things that were, you know, that we I guess allowed to sell were the old ones, the ones that are sort of semi-obsolete,” Trump said in the Fox News interview. “They didn’t even sell that many, the 200s, and the 200s are old now. The Blackwells are very modern, very up to date. In another year, they will be obsolete.”

Trump’s comments may be a welcome sign for US lawmakers who have been pushing Congress to prevent Nvidia from selling Blackwells to China for at least 18 months. Senators Jim Banks, an Indiana Republican, and Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat, have managed to advance their bill, the so-called AI Overwatch Act, into final negotiations for an annual defence package that typically passes in December.

See also: Who gets to own the next Anthropic?

The president’s indication that he doesn’t plan on allowing Nvidia to sell Blackwells to China for another two or three years adds to momentum for a bill that’s also been boosted by Huang’s downfall. His forced resignation removed a long-time foe of stricter US export controls and diminished the chipmaker’s clout on Capitol Hill.

Nvidia’s Blackwell line of AI chips has more recently been succeeded by its newer generation Vera Rubin processors. On Tuesday’s earnings call, Colette Kress, the company’s interim CEO, said the Vera Rubin product launch was the fastest in the chipmaker’s history.

Kress also told analysts that Nvidia had sold US$2.4 billion ($3.1 billion) worth of licensed, Hopper AI products to China in the most recent quarter, after winning Trump’s blessing last year to sell H200 chips to the Asian nation. But she added that the company is no longer shipping Hopper products to China, without elaborating why.

title: Meta to hire new India policy chief to repair frayed ties — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 19): Meta Platforms Inc is scouting for a senior public policy executive in India to mend its fractured relationship with the government of one of its biggest growth markets.

The social media giant is seeking a vice president of public policy, people familiar with the matter said, asking not to be named as the job hasn’t been advertised publicly. Meta representatives didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Senior director Aman Jain currently leads government relations for Meta in India. His position will report to the new vice president of public policy, the people said.

India is the largest market by users for Meta’s Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp with massive headroom for sales growth. The world’s most populous country is also significant for Meta’s artificial intelligence ambitions, offering the company an important testing ground for deploying its open source Llama models to deepen engagement and unlock new monetisation opportunities across its apps.

Yet its relationship with the federal government has faced severe tests. Earlier this year, it announced a new “username” feature on WhatsApp that allowed users globally to connect without exchanging numbers. Meta touted the feature as giving users more privacy, but India’s federal government has so far thwarted its rollout over fears it could fuel online fraud. WhatsApp has more than 650 million users in India and the country’s pushback on the feature imperils its success.

Meta was also caught in the crosshairs of the government over child sexual abuse material on its platforms including Instagram. Meta has since removed more explicit content from Instagram in India. In August, the company’s chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan apologised to Indian officials for temporarily restricting a Facebook post of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

See also: Who gets to own the next Anthropic?

The episodes were widely seen as a failure of Meta’s India public policy team to assuage India’s growing uneasiness with social media platforms that wield enormous influence over its citizens and have been a key tool for the country’s young Gen Z population in anti-government protests this year.

Before Jain, Shivnath Thukral led Meta’s government relations as vice president of public policy. He left the company last year for fintech PhonePe, while Jain joined from Amazon.com Inc this year as senior director. By now hiring a vice president again, Meta is reverting to its old structure as it seeks to bolster the crucial and sensitive function.

Beyond Meta, companies including Google have run into regulatory friction with the Modi administration over IT rules, content and app takedowns. The Alphabet Inc company shook up its India policy team last year, and recently promoted an insider as director of government affairs.

See also: Alibaba’s AI ambitions face steep challenge in US chip controls

Public policy or government affairs roles have increasingly become key to Big Tech’s expansion drive in India. The jobs offer some of the highest compensation at US tech firms’ India offices but can be extremely thorny with a nationalist government at the helm.

Rare success stories include Apple Inc, whose policy team aligned the company with India’s manufacturing ambitions to make the country a key producer of iPhones and a fledgling market where sales have topped US$10 billion.

title: Anthropic raises US$107.3 bil to top SpaceX’s record debut
article:
(Nov 19): Anthropic PBC and its seven co-founders have raised US$107.3 billion ($138.3 billion) in an upsized initial public offering (IPO) and private placement, becoming the first frontier artificial intelligence (AI) lab tapping the public markets to fund its development of thinking machines.

The AI firm sold 956.4 million shares and the co-founders sold 23.6 million shares for US$83 each, according to a statement on Wednesday confirming an earlier Bloomberg News report, above the marketed range. The company had marketed 801.4 million shares, while the co-founders offered 23.6 million shares, in a range of US$70 to US$78 each.

Anthropic shares are indicated to open between 20% and 26% higher across grey-market venues, including the perpetual futures on the Hyperliquid crypto platform.

Anthropic’s debut at a fully diluted valuation of roughly US$1.5 trillion marks a watershed moment for both AI and global financial markets that have become increasingly tied to the technology’s prospects. Investors have begun to expand their focus from primarily backing chipmakers and other infrastructure providers to the makers of platforms such as Claude as they weave themselves into the fabric of business, academia, government and healthcare.

The offering also includes a US$26 billion private placement listed in Anthropic’s filings, with firms including Alphabet Inc’s Google, Advanced Micro Devices Inc (AMD) and Microsoft Corp participating. Anthropic’s IPO is the biggest of all time even without the placement, with the US$81.3 billion base deal topping SpaceX’s at US$75 billion.

Demand for the IPO neared seven times the number of shares available, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday. Buyers from Wall Street to London to Tokyo clamoured for a slice of a stock that is expected to quickly join indices such as the Nasdaq 100 after it begins trading on Thursday. Futures on the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.9% during early Asian hours on Thursday, even as technology shares in Taiwan and South Korea slumped.

See also: The biggest winners in Anthropic’s landmark public offering

Bankers told prospective investors that existing backers would be prioritised by Anthropic, and some would-be buyers would receive smaller allocations than they expect, people familiar with the matter have said.

Some investors are offering a portion of their Anthropic IPO allocation to other prospective backers, letting them collect additional fees and reduce their risk before trading begins, while others with pre-IPO stakes are marketing them to buyers via special purpose vehicles.

Anthropic’s IPO puts it among the 15 largest publicly traded companies by market value, neck and neck with Tesla Inc but ahead of Eli Lilly & Co, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

See also: Enrichment class provider Tafa Holdings files draft prospectus for SGX IPO

The valuation is below the US$2 trillion floated months ago but well above US$1.1 trillion that some on Wall Street suggested in the depths of the recent sell-off in tech stocks.

Anthropic’s listing is the first ever by a frontier AI lab, a cohort of firms building the most advanced models that are intended to tackle difficult problems and assist users in complex tasks such as software design, legal work and scientific discovery. The debut puts the company firmly ahead of rival OpenAI, which is not planning to go public before 2027.

The stock market did not offer a supportive setting for the Claude chatbot maker’s debut, with the Nasdaq 100 Index down 4.4% over the past week through Wednesday’s close. Nvidia Corp extended a losing streak to a fifth day, sinking 2.9% during regular trading, even after the chipmaker reported earnings that beat expectations. It is set to buy US$10 billion of Anthropic stock as part of the private placement.

“We are not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day, or what market conditions we go public into,” Anthropic chief executive officer Dario Amodei, told JPMorgan Chase & Co CEO Jamie Dimon at an event last Friday. He said the best piece of advice he’s gotten throughout the process is, “Never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it’s really worth.”

The debut is set to enhance the personal fortunes of the co-founders, including Amodei, as well as many of Anthropic’s employees. It will also juice returns for its venture capital backers, including Iconiq, Coatue Management and Spark Capital, which has a seat on the board.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Morgan Stanley led Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing showed. The stock is expected to trade on Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.
